newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS TAKE THORNTON WITH TOP OVERALL PICK AT DRAFT.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS TAKE THORNTON WITH TOP OVERALL PICK AT DRAFT.

text.p: The Boston Bruins, picking first for the first time in 15 years, made 17-year-old centre Joe Thornton the top selection in the National Hockey League draft Saturday.

The pick was no surprise. Thornton was the top-rated skater available, according to the NHL's Central Scouting Bureau. He became the first 17-year-old picked first overall since the Buffalo Sabres tabbed Pierre Turgeon in 1987.

Thornton also was the first centre taken with the top pick since the Ottawa Senators chose Alexandre Daigle in 1993. Thornton's selection ended a streak of three years in which a defenceman was the top overall pick.
He will join a Bruins team that failed to make the playoffs for the first time in 30 years.
"Training camp will be the biggest test. I'm ready for training camp," he said. "I have no pressure on me, I just have to get stronger. I was scared, but now I'm glad to be a Bruin."
Nicknamed "Big Bird," the 6-4 (1.93 metres), 198-pound (90 kg) Thornton played junior hockey for the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds of the Ontario Hockey League.

Thornton had 41 goals and 81 assists in only 59 games last season, finishing second in the OHL in points and assists. OHL coaches named him the best faceoff man in his division and he was one of the youngest members of Canada's gold-medal entry at the 1997 World Junior Championships.
"If there's such a thing as a complete hockey player at his age, I think Joe Thornton is," said Frank Bonello, director of NHL Central Scouting.

With the second pick, the San Jose Sharks, who ranked last in the league with 211 goals last season, chose centre Patrick Marleau. He amassed 51 goals and 74 assists for Seattle of the Western Hockey League, but also is an outstanding two-way player with nine shorthanded goals.
Finnish playmaker Olli Jokinen was taken third by the Los Angeles Kings. He was the top-ranked European and had 14 goals and 27 assists in 50 games.
The 18-year-old was the youngest player on his Finnish Elite League team but centred its top line. He also competed at the 1997 world championships, where he was the youngest player.
The New York Islanders surprisingly ended the run on centres by using the fourth pick on goaltender Roberto Luongo. Luongo became the highest netminder selected in draft history.
The Isles talked trade with several teams, but held onto their fifth pick and raised a few more eyebrows by going with defenceman Eric Brewer.
The Calgary Flames gobbled up centre Daniel Tkaczuk with the sixth pick. Ranked third by NHL Central Scouting, he is a gifted playmaker and tenacious penalty-killer.
The Tampa Bay Lightning, one of the teams that tried to move up, settled for defenceman Paul Mara at seventh.
The Bruins used the eighth pick on left wing Sergei Samsonov, who had 29 games as an 18-year-old in the International Hockey League.
Defencemen went on the next two picks -- Nick Boynton to the Washington Capitals at nine and rugged Brad Ference to the Vancouver Canucks.

The next 10 selections were all forwards. The Montreal Canadiens took Jason Ward with the 11th pick, followed by the Ottawa Senators, who went with Slovakian Marian Hossa. Daniel Clearly was still around when the Chicago Blackhawks selected 13th and the Edmonton Oilers made Michael Riesen the first Swiss-trained player ever taken in the first round.
The Kings used their second first-round pick on left wing Matt Zultek, while the Blackhawks went with right wing Ty Jones with their other first-rounder.
The host Pittsburgh Penguins, ignoring chants of "defense, defence," gambled on Slovakian Robert Dome.
The Mighty Ducks of Anaheim chose centre Mikael Holmqvist, the New York Rangers went for right wing Stefan Cherneski and the Florida Panthers tabbed centre Mike Brown to round out the top 20.
The Buffalo Sabres already have the NHL's most valuable goalie in Dominik Hasek, but used the 21st pick on Finnish netminder Mika Noronen.
The Carolina Hurricanes had the next two picks and used the 22nd selection on defenceman Nikos Tselios, cousin of three-time Norris Trophy winner Chris Chelios.

Carolina traded the 23rd pick to San Jose, which went for another defenceman, Scott Hannan. The New Jersey Devils selected goaltender Jean-Francois Damphousse at 24, Dallas went for left wing Brenden Morrow and the Colorado Avalanche ended the first round with defenceman Kevin Grimes.
The Stanley Cup champion Detroit Red Wings, Philadelphia Flyers, Phoenix Coyotes, St. Louis Blues and Toronto Maple Leafs did not have picks in the first round.
There were three other draft-day trades, two of them involving the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Calgary re-acquired goaltender Rick Tabaracci from Tampa Bay for a 1998 fourth-round pick. The Sharks obtained veteran forward Shawn Burr from the Lightning for a second-round pick this year and a third-rounder in 1998.
The New York Rangers added some muscle by acquiring Mike Peluso from the St. Louis Blues for future considerations.
